subject: Request: Exec signoff for 4yr price commitment + midterm reset clause
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Betsy Cole <betsy@healthsync.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Exec signoff for 4yr price commitment + midterm reset clause

Team — attaching the latest term sheet and MAUP analysis for HealthSync. Quick context: HealthSync is prepared to commit to a 4-year reserved capacity contract with ~60% of forecasted throughputs reserved up-front. They requested two non-standard asks that require executive signoff: a) a price lock for the full 48 months with a midterm reset mechanism at month 24 limited to a maximum uplift (uplift cap), and b) an explicit renewal-protection clause that prevents unilateral price increases beyond the uplift cap during the initial renewal negotiation window.

Highlights / recommended stance: 
- Base: list pricing with a 28% committed discount off list for the reserved capacity band they selected.
- Uplift mechanics: a midterm reset at month 24 tied to an agreed index (CPI-U + 0.5%), but capped at +3.0 percentage points above year-1 effective rate; any positive reset must be agreed by both parties and is limited to capacity bands in-scope.
- Renewal protection: for the first renewal window (months 42–48) Customer receives a price protection right: Redwood may propose adjustments, but increases over the capped uplift require Executive approval and will trigger a rollback option for the customer if not mutually agreed.
- Out: We retain a 90-day notice and an early-termination fee (pro-rated) tied to remaining committed spend.

Why approve: this trade gives us 4 years of committed revenue and predictable utilization patterns that materially reduce peak-handling costs. The revenue model shows ~22% improvement in blended unit economics vs. pay-as-you-go over the same period. The midterm reset gives us a limited path to adjust to macro cost shifts while the cap and renewal protection strike a balance customers seek.

Request: Executive signoff to permit these two non-standard terms (price lock + midterm reset with +3.0% cap; renewal-protection mechanics as drafted). If approved, we will issue the term sheet to HealthSync and arrange legal to prepare redlines.

Attachments: redwood_term_sheet_v4.pdf (term sheet), healthsync_maup_analysis.xlsx (volume/MAUP sensitivity).

Thanks —
David
David Kim
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Betsy Cole <betsy@healthsync.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exec signoff for 4yr price commitment + midterm reset clause

David — I reviewed the term sheet. A few questions before I can greenlight: 
1) The +3.0 percentage point cap: is that absolute percentage points on the effective unit price, or relative to the discount band? Need clarity (e.g., 28% discount -> does cap mean discount can only worsen to 25%?).
2) What are the trigger conditions for the midterm reset? You wrote CPI-U + 0.5% but we should clarify whether a reset is automatic or requires mutual agreement to execute the reset math. 
3) Renewal rollback: detail the exact rollback mechanism and operational implications (credits, termination right, transition support). Legal will want deterministic calculations.

I like the economics but want firm language so Legal and Finance can model downside. Please add a short example calc for year 1 -> year 3 showing numbers under floor/median/ceiling scenarios. 

If we can get those clarified today I can escalate to exec signoff.

Laura
VP, Head of Revenue Operations
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Betsy Cole <betsy@healthsync.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exec signoff for 4yr price commitment + midterm reset clause

Laura / David — I updated the spreadsheet and attached three scenarios in a single tab: conservative, base, aggressive. Quick answers inline: 
- Cap interpretation: the +3.0 point cap refers to absolute percentage points on the effective discount vs year-1 effective discount. Example attached (see calc rows 45–60): Year-1 effective discount = 28%; maximum allowed discount at reset = 31% (i.e., discount cannot worsen more than 3 points). Conversely, if market improves we can reduce discount but we will not propose more than +3 point worsening.
- Reset trigger: Reset is "mutual-proposal" only — either party can request recalculation; if both parties agree we apply the CPI-U + 0.5% formula to the baseline rate and then clamp by the +3pt cap. If parties cannot agree, no automatic unilateral change occurs.
- Renewal rollback: If at renewal Redwood proposes an increase beyond the capped uplift and parties cannot reach agreement within the 30-day negotiation window, customer gains a one-time right to (a) accept prior-year pricing for the first 12 months of renewal, or (b) terminate with a 120-day wind-down and a pro-rata refund of pre-paid reserved spend. Legal asked that we replace the word "rollback" with "conditional renewal protection" and add deterministic calculations — included in the attached tab.

I'll fold these clarifications into the term sheet and send a redline to Legal. If Execs are comfortable with the mutual-proposal reset and the +3pt clamp, this should be signable.

Marissa
Director, Deal Desk Operations
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

I approve the non-standard terms as described (mutual-proposal midterm reset; CPI-U + 0.5% formula; absolute +3.0 percentage point clamp on discount drift; conditional renewal protection per the calculation table). Please proceed: instruct Legal to prepare final contract redlines and coordinate DocuSign.
